Explain what DNS does when you open a website to someone with no technical background.
Limits: at most 170 words. Include one analogy, on a line starting with 'Analogy:', and one worked example, on a line starting with 'Example:'. Mention the IP address.
Answer with the explanation only.

arguments.answer:
When you type a website name like "example.com", your computer can't use that name directly. Computers find each other using numbers called IP addresses, which work like a street address for every machine on the internet. DNS (Domain Name System) is the service that turns the easy-to-remember name into the right IP address.

Analogy: DNS is like the contacts app on your phone. You tap "Mom", and the phone looks up her number and dials it for you, so you never have to memorize it.

Example: You type "www.wikipedia.org" into your browser. Your computer asks a DNS server, "What's the address for wikipedia.org?" The server answers with an IP address such as 208.80.154.224. Your browser then connects to that address and the page loads, usually in a fraction of a second.

Your computer also remembers recent answers for a while, so websites you visit often can open even faster. Without DNS, you would have to memorize a string of numbers for every website you use.
